title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: whyna implements typed/informative missingness R, letting track values missing. Standard R treats missing values identical NAs, losing critical information missingness mechanism. package introduces custom vector class stores observed value (NA) reason ’s missing, following Rubin’s (1976) MCAR/MAR/MNAR framework.

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
code: # Install from GitHub: devtools::install_github("brownag/whyna")

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: real data, missing values arise different mechanisms, distinct mathematical inferential properties. Rubin’s (1976) taxonomy formalizes via conditional probability missingness given complete data. MCAR (Missing Completely Random) Missingness independent observed unobserved data. Safe delete; standard listwise deletion yields unbiased estimates. MAR (Missing Random) Missingness depends observed data unobserved value . mechanism ignorable: valid inference requires maximum likelihood multiple imputation (MI) methods, without explicitly modelling missingness process. MNAR (Missing Random) Missingness depends unobserved value . mechanism non-ignorable: standard analysis methods introduce severe bias. Sensitivity analysis specialized methods (selection models, pattern-mixture models) required.

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: missingness mechanism ignorable analyst can obtain valid parameter estimates without explicitly modelling missingness process. holds : 1. data MAR, 2. missingness parameters distinct data-generating parameters (cross-constraints). ignorability, standard likelihood-based inference proceeds normally. MNAR violates ignorability, forcing analysts model missingness mechanism directly.

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: R uses three-valued logic: TRUE, FALSE, NA (unknown). NA appears comparison, result NA truth value determined. correct behavior. alternative—treating NA extreme value (smallest largest number)—produces silent errors. NA treated maximum value, age > 65 incorrectly include missing ages result set. NA minimum value, exclude . result silently reports something untrue. R whyna preserve three-valued logic. filter compare, NA propagates naturally, must explicitly handle .na() na.rm = TRUE. forces confront missing data rather accidentally corrupting analysis.
code: NA > 65          # returns NA, not TRUE or FALSE is.na(NA > 65)   # TRUE

code: library(whyna)  measurements <- why_na(   c(5.2, NA, 7.1, NA, 3.8),   type = c(0L, 1L, 0L, 2L, 3L)  # 0=Observed, 1=MCAR, 2=MAR, 3=MNAR )  measurements #> <informative_na<double>[5]> #> [1] 5.2       <NA:MCAR> 7.1       <NA:MAR>  <NA:MNAR>  # Extract missingness predicates is_mcar(measurements) #> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE  is_mar(measurements) #> [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE  is_mnar(measurements) #> [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  # Get a summary factor missing_reason(measurements) #> [1] Observed MCAR     Observed MAR      MNAR     #> Levels: Observed MCAR MAR MNAR

what: Generalized Typed NA: Beyond Numeric Data
title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: whyna now supports vector type, just doubles. ’s example character data sentinel codes (like “LOD” “limit detection”) normal values coexist: Integer example type preservation:
code: # Character example: lab measurement codes lab_results <- c("42.5", "LOD", "38.2", "NULL-broken", "45.1") measurements <- sentinel_recode(   lab_results,   map = list("LOD" = "MNAR", "NULL-broken" = "MCAR"),   ptype = character() )  measurements #> <informative_na<character>[5]> #> [1] 42.5      <NA:MNAR> 38.2      <NA:MCAR> 45.1 missing_reason(measurements) #> [1] Observed MNAR     Observed MCAR     Observed #> Levels: Observed MCAR MAR MNAR counts <- why_na(c(10L, NA, 5L, NA, 8L), c(0L, 1L, 0L, 2L, 0L)) counts  # Type is preserved: integer, not double #> <informative_na<integer>[5]> #> [1] 10        <NA:MCAR>  5        <NA:MAR>   8

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: Suppose ’re analyzing dissolved oxygen () measurements 50 water samples:
code: library(whyna) library(tibble) library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)  # Simulated water quality dataset set.seed(123) n <- 50  water_data <- tibble(   site_id = 1:n,   do_value = c(rnorm(35, mean = 8, sd = 1), rep(NA_real_, 15)),   do_type = c(rep(0L, 35), rep(1L, 5), rep(3L, 10)),   site_type = sample(c("upstream", "downstream"), n, replace = TRUE),   temperature = rnorm(n, mean = 15, sd = 3),   ph = rnorm(n, mean = 7.5, sd = 0.5) )  # Now create the typed missing-data vector water_data <- water_data |>   mutate(     do = why_na(do_value, type = do_type)   ) |>   select(site_id, do, site_type, temperature, ph)  water_data #> # A tibble: 50 × 5 #>    site_id        do site_type  temperature    ph #>      <int> <why_dbl> <chr>            <dbl> <dbl> #>  1       1  7.439524 downstream        16.1  7.21 #>  2       2  7.769823 upstream          13.5  7.80 #>  3       3  9.558708 upstream          14.0  6.69 #>  4       4  8.070508 upstream          11.9  7.47 #>  5       5  8.129288 upstream          11.8  7.76 #>  6       6  9.715065 downstream        15.9  7.65 #>  7       7  8.460916 downstream        16.3  7.55 #>  8       8  6.734939 upstream          15.2  7.18 #>  9       9  7.313147 downstream        17.8  7.08 #> 10      10  7.554338 downstream        21.2  6.99 #> # ℹ 40 more rows

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: 1. Describe missingness patterns 2. Filter missingness mechanism sensitivity analysis 3. Stratified analysis site type 4. Extract complete-case subset (removes missing, regardless type)
code: water_data |>   summarise(     n_obs = sum(!is.na(do)),     n_mcar = sum(is_mcar(do)),     n_mar = sum(is_mar(do)),     n_mnar = sum(is_mnar(do))   ) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   n_obs n_mcar n_mar n_mnar #>   <int>  <int> <int>  <int> #> 1    35      5     0     10 # Rows with observed data only observed <- water_data |> filter(!is.na(do)) nrow(observed) #> [1] 35  # Rows with observed or MCAR (safe to use) trustworthy <- water_data |> filter(!is.na(do) | is_mcar(do)) nrow(trustworthy) #> [1] 40  # Check for MNAR (biasing mechanism) any(is_mnar(water_data$do)) #> [1] TRUE water_data |>   group_by(site_type) |>   summarise(     n = n(),     mean_do = mean(as.double(do), na.rm = TRUE),     pct_mnar = 100 * mean(is_mnar(do)),     .groups = "drop"   ) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   site_type      n mean_do pct_mnar #>   <chr>      <int>   <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 downstream    28    8.16     25   #> 2 upstream      22    7.89     13.6 complete <- water_data |> filter(!is.na(do)) nrow(complete) #> [1] 35 head(complete) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   site_id        do site_type  temperature    ph #>     <int> <why_dbl> <chr>            <dbl> <dbl> #> 1       1  7.439524 downstream        16.1  7.21 #> 2       2  7.769823 upstream          13.5  7.80 #> 3       3  9.558708 upstream          14.0  6.69 #> 4       4  8.070508 upstream          11.9  7.47 #> 5       5  8.129288 upstream          11.8  7.76 #> 6       6  9.715065 downstream        15.9  7.65

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: why_na(x, type = NULL) User-facing constructor. Auto-detects missingness type omitted. informative_na(x, type = NULL) Alias why_na() (verbose form, identical behavior). new_informative_na(value, type) Low-level constructor; strict validation, developers.
code: why_na(c(1.5, NA, 2.3)) #> <informative_na<double>[3]> #> [1] 1.5       <NA:MCAR> 2.3

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: is_mcar(x), is_mar(x), is_mnar(x) Logical masks indicating elements given missingness type. missing_reason(x) Returns factor levels: Observed, MCAR, MAR, MNAR. is_observed(x), is_ignorable(x) Additional predicates analysis workflows. missing_summary(x) Quick overview missingness patterns: returns data.frame mechanism counts proportions.
code: x <- why_na(c(1, NA, 3, NA), c(0L, 1L, 0L, 2L)) is_mcar(x) #> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE is_mar(x) #> [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE missing_reason(x) #> [1] Observed MCAR     Observed MAR      #> Levels: Observed MCAR MAR MNAR is_observed(x) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE is_ignorable(x) #> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE missing_summary(x) #>   mechanism n proportion #> 1  Observed 2       0.50 #> 2      MCAR 1       0.25 #> 3       MAR 1       0.25 #> 4      MNAR 0       0.00

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: sentinel_recode(x, map) Maps domain-specific sentinel codes (e.g., "-9999", "LOD", "NULL-broken") whyna vector. Numeric values pass observed.
code: raw <- c("12.5", "-9999", "LOD", "15.1") x <- sentinel_recode(raw, list("-9999" = "MAR", "LOD" = "MNAR")) x #> <informative_na<double>[4]> #> [1] 12.5      <NA:MAR>  <NA:MNAR> 15.1

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: .na(x) Returns TRUE missing entries (regardless type). format(x), print(x) Displays observed values numerically missing <NA:MCAR>, etc. c(), rbind() Combines plain numeric vectors, upgrading informative_na. Cast double Extracts value field (lossy; discards type information).
code: x <- why_na(c(1.5, NA), c(0L, 1L)) y <- c(3.1, 4.2) c(x, y) #> <informative_na<double>[4]> #> [1] 1.5       <NA:MCAR> 3.1       4.2 as.double(x) #> [1] 1.5  NA

title: Informative Missingness via vctrs Records
text: Immutability types: type != 0L, value field always NA appropriate type (e.g., NA_integer_ integer vectors, NA_character_ character, <NA> factors). Type preservation: Input type preserved why_na(). Use optional ptype argument explicit casting. vctrs foundation: Built vctrs::new_rcrd() integration tidyverse (dplyr, tibble). arithmetic: Operations like x + 1 return standard NA (class-preserving). Types preserved subsetting revert standard NA arithmetic operations.

title: Recode sentinel codes to whyna vector — sentinel_recode
text: x character numeric vector containing raw data sentinel codes. map named list mapping sentinel strings mechanism types. Values must "MCAR", "MAR", "MNAR". Example: list("-9999" = "MAR", "LOD" = "MNAR", "NULL-broken" = "MCAR"). ptype prototype vector. Non-sentinel values x cast type. Default double() backward compatibility; use integer(), character(), .Date(NA) types.
